newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rate hopes hoist Australian stocks higher by close.
newsitem.headline: Rate hopes hoist Australian stocks higher by close.

text.p: Hopes of an interest rate cut hoisted Australian shares higher by the close on Monday although trade remained lacklustre as players awaited the result of the Reserve Bank's deliberations on Tuesday.
The All Ordinaries index rose 18.1 points to 2357.5.

With the recent spate of economic data sparking speculation of when, rather than if, interest rates would be cut, those traders willing to play the game pushed the market solidly higher in the afternoon session.
"That's what it seems to be related to," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne brokerage Peake Lands Kirwan.

"There is a possibility of the Reserve Bank will make their announcement tomorrow (Tuesday) about an interest rate cut, if any, and that has had a beneficial effect on the banks, all of which are up quite strongly," he said.

Lourey said the market seemed to be viewing a Clinton win in the U.S. presidential elections as favourable. "I think everybody is expecting a Clinton victory in the U.S. and they believe that will be good for the market," he said.

Star performer was Westpac Banking Corp which went to record highs after it announced a plan to buy back up to five percent of its shares. Brokers said the buyback underpinned a share price already receiving strong support from takeover talk.
Westpac closed 20 cents higher at A$7.38 (US$5.83) after touching A$7.40.
Papua New Guinea-based Orogen Minerals moved ahead and again saw active trade in its second day as a listed company.
Orogen closed five cents up at A$2.17 with more than 11.5 million shares traded.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
